symbols.note: copied from `gatekit symbols system <name> --dll dx11 --full` (addresses are bg3_dx11.exe; methods without an address were not found in the game binary and are listed with address null). Parsed by script from the command output, not retyped.
symbols.limits: reads/writes: the component views in the parameters of the system's exported methods. uses: the component operations (add, remove, get, has) its per-frame update performs through the engine's out-of-line helpers, itself or in a function it calls (depth 2), with the call site; kind index: a matched method reads the type's index and the operation is not known. Not listed: operations the compiler inlined, those deeper than depth 2, and what a method that is not the update does (e.g. a SystemLoad) - read its pseudo-code; an empty writes list is not "writes nothing".

does.text: After the summoned entity has been made and put into the caster's summon container, CreateSummon looks at the request record it was given and adds up to three one-frame request components to the NEW summon entity, each with its own guard. (1) If the summon description says the summon is to be added to an existing concentration (and the spell is not one whose prototype carries the concentration flag, which takes a different branch and adds a spell-carrying request instead), it adds esv::summon::AddToExistingConcentrationRequestOneFrameComponent holding the owner's handle plus a true byte. (2) If the description's apply-late-join-penalty flag is set it adds esv::summon::LateJoinPenaltyOneFrameComponent (a tag, no payload). (3) If the description carries a valid projectile handle it adds esv::summon::AttachToProjectileRequestOneFrameComponent holding that handle. It also adds UseCasterPassivesComponent when the use-caster-passives flag is set. (Review 2026-11-14 (Opus): the spell-carrying branch is taken whenever the summon's spell id is valid and byte +0x10 of the record at description+0xA0 has bit 0x40, whatever the add-to-existing-concentration flag says; the AddToExistingConcentration request is the else branch, so it needs that flag and either an invalid spell id or the bit clear. Reading bit 0x40 as 'concentration' is a guess from the request it leads to. Before these, CreateSummon also adds eoc::summon::AnimationComponent to every new summon unconditionally (EoCServer.dll+0x7B72D0 -> +0x7B7900, type name resolved through its initialiser).)
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll (Toolkit build, named) esv::summon::SpawnSystem::CreateSummon +0x7BDF70, read in 245 lines of pseudo-code around every AddComponent. The adder helpers each call SetupComponentFrameStorage: EoCServer.dll+0x7B7AF0 (type index resolved by its initialiser to AttachToProjectileRequestOneFrameComponent), +0x7B7220 -> +0x7B7700 (type index DAT_18221fa54 resolved by its initialiser to AddToExistingConcentrationRequestOneFrameComponent), +0x7B7430 -> +0x7B86F0 (type index DAT_18221f994, initialiser names LateJoinPenaltyOneFrameComponent), +0x7B9120 (UseCasterPassivesComponent). The flags' meaning was cross-checked against the Script Extender's SummonDesc layout (bytes +0xC1 AddToExistingConcentration, +0xC2 ApplyLateJoinPenalty, +0xC3 UseCasterPassives, +0xF0 AttachToProjectile), which fit the offsets read in the code. dx11 side: ProcessCreateSummon (the queue dispatcher that calls CreateSummon) is bg3_dx11.exe+0x2DCC680; CreateSummon itself was read in EoCServer.dll, its dx11 address was not located.

does.text: The per-frame step that drains the queued summon requests (SummonDesc records filed by RequestCreateSummon) and hands each to CreateSummon; it does not add components itself in the part read.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll+0x7C0010 (323 lines read by grep for adds/removes and calls); bg3_dx11.exe+0x2DCC680 is the same function in the game.
